{"parts":[{"part_id":"Q3","solution":"Principle: in free fall (negligible air resistance) the only force on the ball is gravity, so by Newton's second law its acceleration is a = g = 9.8 m/s^2 downward at every point of the flight.
On the way up the velocity is upward and decreasing; on the way down it is downward.
At the highest point the velocity changes from upward to downward, so at that instant v = 0.
The acceleration there is still g, pointing down. It is not zero, since the velocity is still changing.
Therefore v = 0 and a points down, which is choice (B).","answer":{"choices":["B"],"value":null,"unit":null,"rel_tol":null,"accept_also":[],"expression":null,"elements":[],"must_include":[]},"uses":[],"alternatives":[]}]}

{"parts":[{"part_id":"Q4.a","solution":"Identify every external force on the crate (free-body diagram).
Gravity: weight mg = 4.0*10 = 40 N, pointing straight down.
Floor: normal force N, pointing straight up; since the rope is horizontal and there is no vertical acceleration, N = mg = 40 N.
Rope: tension T = 20 N, pointing to the right.
Floor: kinetic friction f = mu*N = 0.25*40 = 10 N, pointing to the left, opposite the motion.
Draw each force as an arrow starting on the dot. The weight and normal arrows are equal in length, and the friction arrow is half the length of the tension arrow.","answer":{"choices":[],"value":null,"unit":null,"rel_tol":null,"accept_also":[],"expression":null,"elements":[{"label":"F_g (weight, mg)","kind":"force","direction":"down","position":"starts on the dot"},{"label":"F_N (normal force)","kind":"force","direction":"up","position":"starts on the dot"},{"label":"T (tension)","kind":"force","direction":"right","position":"starts on the dot"},{"label":"f_k (kinetic friction)","kind":"force","direction":"left","position":"starts on the dot"}],"must_include":["Exactly four forces are drawn, with no components and no extra forces such as a 'net force' or an 'applied force' in addition to tension.","Each arrow starts on the dot and is labeled."]},"uses":[],"alternatives":[]},{"part_id":"Q4.b","solution":"Apply Newton's second law along the horizontal direction.
Vertical balance gives the normal force: N = mg = 4.0*10 = 40 N.
Kinetic friction: f = mu*N = 0.25*40 = 10 N, acting to the left.
Net horizontal force: F_net = T - f = 20 - 10 = 10 N, to the right.
Acceleration: a = F_net/m = 10/4.0 = 2.5 m/s^2.","answer":{"choices":[],"value":2.5,"unit":"m/s^2","rel_tol":null,"accept_also":[],"expression":null,"elements":[],"must_include":[]},"uses":[],"alternatives":[]},{"part_id":"Q4.c","solution":"Once the rope is cut, the tension force disappears.
The crate is still sliding, so kinetic friction f = mu*mg = 10 N still acts on it, opposite the velocity (to the left).
The weight and the normal force still balance each other.
The net force is therefore 10 N to the left, opposite the motion.
The acceleration is a = 10/4.0 = 2.5 m/s^2, directed to the left.
The crate keeps moving to the right but slows down at a constant rate until it stops.
Once stopped, there is no horizontal force trying to move it, so friction becomes zero and the crate stays at rest.","answer":{"choices":[],"value":null,"unit":null,"rel_tol":null,"accept_also":[],"expression":null,"elements":[],"must_include":["The crate continues moving to the right while slowing down, then comes to rest.","After the cut, tension no longer acts, so the only horizontal force is kinetic friction.","Friction acts opposite the motion (to the left), so the net force opposes the velocity and causes deceleration.","The deceleration is constant, because friction is constant (mu*mg = 10 N), giving 2.5 m/s^2."]},"uses":["Q4.b"],"alternatives":[]}]}

{"parts":[{"part_id":"Q5.a","solution":"Method: completing the square.
Half of the x-coefficient: -6/2 = -3, and (-3)^2 = 9.
f(x) = x^2 - 6x + 9 - 9 + 5
f(x) = (x - 3)^2 - 4
So h = 3 and k = -4.","answer":{"choices":[],"value":null,"unit":null,"rel_tol":null,"accept_also":[],"expression":"(x - 3)^2 - 4","elements":[],"must_include":[]},"uses":[],"alternatives":[]},{"part_id":"Q5.b","solution":"From part (a), f(x) = (x - 3)^2 - 4.
A square is never negative, so (x - 3)^2 >= 0, with equality at x = 3.
Therefore f(x) >= -4.
The minimum value is f(3) = -4, attained at x = 3.","answer":{"choices":[],"value":-4,"unit":null,"rel_tol":null,"accept_also":[],"expression":null,"elements":[],"must_include":[]},"uses":["Q5.a"],"alternatives":[]},{"part_id":"Q5.c","solution":"From part (a), the vertex form is f(x) = (x - 3)^2 - 4, so the vertex is (3, -4).
The leading coefficient is positive, so the parabola opens upward.

The x-intercepts are (1, 0) and (5, 0).
y-intercept: f(0) = 5, giving (0, 5).
The axis of symmetry is x = 3.
